source.label: Wikipedia: Petrarch's Virgil (title page), c. 1336; Petrarch became Simone's friend in Avignon
Wikipedia: Simone also worked as a miniaturist; the frontispiece of the Codex Ambrosianus

highlight.text: It was on vellum that Simone traced the features of Laura, and a page illuminated by him is still to be seen in a manuscript of Virgil in the Ambrosian Library

source.label: Wikipedia: Simone Martini, Duccio's pupil, is among the Sienese school's most important artists

work.text: Simone Martini, originally from Siena, primarily produced large-scale paintings but also worked as a miniaturist. One of his notable works includes the frontispiece of the Codex Ambrosianus, which he painted around 1340 for Petrarch.

if it be conceded that Simone painted miniatures, as some infer from the sonnet of Petrarch, a Virgil with pictorial ornaments in the Ambrosiana at Milan may be taken as a better illustration of his peculiar style than any other of the same kind.

source.author: J. A. Crowe and G. B. Cavalcaselle
source.title: A History of Painting in Italy, vol. 3: The Sienese School of the Fourteenth Century (ed. Langton Douglas)

moment.text: Very great, then, was that good-fortune of Simone, to live at the time of Messer Francesco Petrarca and to chance to find that most amorous poet at the Court of Avignon

source.author: Giorgio Vasari
source.title: Life of Simone Sanese, in Lives of the Most Eminent Painters, Sculptors and Architects, vol. 1 (trans. Gaston du C. de Vere)

moment.text: … at the papal court of Avignon. There he made the acquaintance of Petrarch, and, it is supposed, of Laura, whose likeness he drew.

source.author: J. A. Crowe and G. B. Cavalcaselle
source.title: A History of Painting in Italy, vol. 3: The Sienese School of the Fourteenth Century (ed. Langton Douglas)

matters.text: But Simon sure, in Paradise the blest, Whence came this noble lady of my heart, Saw her, and took this wond'rous counterpart Which should on earth her lovely face attest.
matters.lead: Petrarch, on the portrait of Laura that Simone painted for him (now lost):

source.author: Francesco Petrarca
source.title: Sonnet LVII, “Per mirar Policleto” (trans. MacGregor), in The Sonnets, Triumphs, and Other Poems of Petrarch

matters.text: whence it may be concluded that Petrarch, who received this precious MS. in 1338, requested of Simone this mark of his friendship, to render it more valuable.

source.author: Thomas Campbell
source.title: Life of Petrarch, in The Sonnets, Triumphs, and Other Poems of Petrarch
